result.topic_en: Euler finds the roots of the transcendental frequency equation for a vibrating elastic lamina: the root ζ = 0, approximate positive roots near (5/2)ϱ, (9/2)ϱ, (13/2)ϱ, (17/2)ϱ with a small correction ω for the first, and he begins to check whether negative roots exist.
result.transcription:
474 DE MOTV VIBRATORIO
Hinc ſtatim patet ſatisfacere $\zeta = 0$, quo ipſe ſtatus aequilibrii continetur. Deinde vero valores idonei pro $\zeta$ continuo propius accedent ad hos angulos
$\frac{5}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{9}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{13}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{17}{2}\varrho$ etc.
ſi enim ponamus $\zeta = \frac{5}{2}\varrho - \omega$ erit Tangens $\zeta = \frac{1-\omega}{1+\omega}$ proxime, cui aequalis eſſe debet formula
$\frac{1 - e^{-5\varrho + 2\omega}}{1 + e^{-5\varrho + 2\omega}}$, ita vt ſit $\omega = \frac{e^{2\omega}}{e^{5\varrho}}$
ſicque propemodum
$\omega = \frac{1}{e^{5\varrho}} = 0,0003882$
atque propius
$\omega = 0,0003885$,
pro ſequentibus caſibus autem hanc correctionem $\omega$ penitus negligere licebit, ita vt iſti valores pro $\zeta$ ſint
I. $\zeta = \frac{5}{2}\varrho - \omega = 3,92666$
II. $\zeta = \frac{9}{2}\varrho \quad = 7,06858$
III. $\zeta = \frac{13}{2}\varrho \quad = 10,21017$
IV. $\zeta = \frac{17}{2}\varrho \quad = 13,35176$
etc.
videamus autem an etiam dentur valores negatiui, quem in finem ponamus $\zeta = -\eta$ eſſeque oportebit
$-\mathrm{Tang.}\,\eta = \frac{e^{-\eta} - e^{+\eta}}{e^{-\eta} + e^{+\eta}}$; ſiue $\mathrm{Tang.}\,\eta = \frac{e^{+\eta} - e^{-\eta}}{e^{\eta} + e^{-\eta}}$,
quae aequatio cum praecedente conuenit, ita vt illi inuenti valores etiam pro $\eta$ valeant, ſicque valores ipſius

items.quote: Hinc ſtatim patet ſatisfacere $\zeta = 0$, quo ipſe ſtatus aequilibrii continetur.
items.english: Hence it is immediately clear that ζ = 0 satisfies the equation, which represents the state of equilibrium itself.

items.quote:
Deinde vero valores idonei pro $\zeta$ continuo propius accedent ad hos angulos
$\frac{5}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{9}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{13}{2}\varrho;\ \frac{17}{2}\varrho$ etc.
items.english: Further, the suitable values for ζ approach ever more closely these angles: (5/2)ϱ, (9/2)ϱ, (13/2)ϱ, (17/2)ϱ, etc.

items.quote: pro ſequentibus caſibus autem hanc correctionem $\omega$ penitus negligere licebit
items.english: For the following cases, however, this correction ω may be entirely neglected.

items.quote: videamus autem an etiam dentur valores negatiui
items.english: Let us see, however, whether negative values also exist.
